lead.hed: Theodore Roosevelt's masters-at-arms fired the fantail guns while underway in the 7th Fleet
lead.insight: DVIDS posted this morning a live-fire aboard USS Theodore Roosevelt on Oct. 11. Master-at-Arms 2nd Class Taylor Bendig and Master-at-Arms Seaman Torres Contreras fired an M240B machine gun from the fantail, and a second frame shows Master-at-Arms 1st Class Jean Loquias reloading a .50-caliber. The caption says Roosevelt, flagship of Carrier Strike Group 9, is underway on routine operations in the U.S. 7th Fleet area. The release is a photo caption, not an operations order, so it does not say where in the 7th Fleet the ship is steaming.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist Seaman Kellie Given · DVIDS 10006894 · Public domain · Master-at-Arms 2nd Class Taylor Bendig and Master-at-Arms Seaman Torres Contreras fire an M240B from the fantail of USS Theodore Roosevelt during a live-fire exercise. Photo taken Oct. 11, 2026.

political.hed: Law & Liberty says the war with Iran is being run on one man's judgment
political.insight: Monday's essay says the strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities in the summer of 2025, and the bombardment that restarted Feb. 28, show a president starting a war without consulting Congress. It notes the 1973 War Powers Resolution has been treated as unconstitutional by every administration since, and calls it ineffective. The piece asks whether Congress can reclaim control of war-making. It is an argument, not a bill or a floor vote.

political.hed: Heritage says states still have to do the work of securing elections
political.insight: Friday's commentary says Americans cannot treat election security as settled. The writer argues the right to vote is not self-executing, and that laws have to administer it and defend it against error, fraud, and foreign interference. It is a call for state administration, not a new federal statute posted with the piece.

tech.hed: The Army took delivery of its first mobile cannon to replace the M777
tech.insight: Defense News reported Monday that the Army has taken delivery of its first Korean-made mobile tactical cannon, less than a year after the solicitation. Brig. Gen. Robert J. Mikesh Jr., the offensive fires portfolio executive, told reporters ahead of the Association of the United States Army meeting that the Hanwha system was on display at an Army Modernization Day on Capitol Hill earlier this month, and that the service wants to test it and get soldier feedback. The August prototyping contract runs four years and up to nearly $263 million, covering as many as 18 systems, with the first six on an accelerated schedule. The cannon is based on the K9, and Hanwha is building an integration site in Opelika, Alabama. This is a prototype in hand, not a fielded replacement.

tech.hed: Vector and Nammo said they will scale munitions for small drones
tech.insight: Defense News reported Monday that Vector and Nammo Defense Systems expanded a partnership, announced at the Association of the United States Army meeting, to integrate munitions into small drones for U.S. military use. The companies first paired Nammo's munitions with Vector's unmanned aircraft earlier this year. Vector chief executive Andy Yakulis said the systems will be produced at scale. Vector supplies an electronic safe-and-arm device that sits between the drone and the munition, and the company has a drone on the Defense Department's Blue List. This is a company announcement, not a contract award.

culture.hed: First Things reports from an Armenian village that says it will fight for its churches
culture.insight: Monday's essay is a dispatch from Svarants, a village in Syunik in southern Armenia, where the writer says Azerbaijan's president has threatened for years to take the region. He writes that Azerbaijan has already expelled Christian residents and bulldozed churches and cemeteries in other parts of historic Armenia, and quotes the village leader saying his people will fight. The piece treats Armenian Christianity, dating to the year 301, as the core of national identity. It is a reported essay, not a government statement.

culture.hed: WORLD reviews Sorkin's Facebook film as a journalism thriller with a paywall of its own
culture.insight: Thursday's review covers Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning, a follow-on to The Social Network, set around the 2021 Facebook Files. The readable opening quotes a Wall Street Journal reporter telling a Facebook employee that a story is not facts. WORLD rates the film R and in theaters. The rest of the review sits behind the magazine's subscription wall, so this item stops at what the public page actually shows.

watch.hed: CENTCOM says it disabled a cargo ship trying to run the Iran blockade on Saturday
watch.note: DVIDS, posted Saturday. A fighter struck the stern of Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman on Oct. 10 after warnings. The release says four ships disabled and 135 turned around since July 14. Held from the lead because the page carries no official still.
